{{Short description|American physicist (1932–2026)}}
'''Nicholas Anthony Krall''' (February 16, 1932 – January 17, 2026) was an American theoretical plasma physicist. He authored over 160 science publications<ref>ISI web of knowledge, search: Nicholas Anthony Krall, June 2013</ref> and contributed to the fields of electron scattering, plasma stability, high energy nuclear physics and magnetohydrodynamics. Krall worked at [[General Atomics]], the [[University of California, San Diego]], the [[Naval Research Laboratory]] and [[University of Maryland]].<ref name="American">American Men and Women of Science 21st Edition (2003)</ref>

== Life and career ==
Krall was born in Kansas City on February 16, 1932. He is the son of Catherine Krall, and her husband Nicholas J. Krall. He received his BS in physics from the [[University of Notre Dame]] in 1954 and his PhD in [[theoretical physics]] from [[Cornell]] University in 1959.  After graduation, Dr. Krall worked as a staff scientist and a manager at [[General Atomics]] in San Diego until 1967.  He worked closely with physicist [[Marshall Rosenbluth]].<ref>"Stabilization of Hot Electron Plasma by a Cold Background" N Krall, Phys. Fluids 9, 820 (1966)</ref><ref>M. N. Rosenbluth, N. A. Krall, and N. Rostoker, Nucl. Fusion Suppl. Pt. 1, 143 (1962)</ref>  After general atomics he accepted a position as professor of physics at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]] in 1967 and held that position for six years.<ref>"Self-Consistent Calculation of an Explosive Instability" Seishi Hamasaki and Nicholas A. Krall Phys. Fluids 14, 1441 (1971)</ref>  While at Maryland he was appointed director joint program for plasma physics, at the [[Naval Research Laboratory]].  He held that position until 1973.  He also co-wrote a textbook<ref>Principles of plasma physics, Volumes 0-911351, Nicholas Krall and Alvin Trivelpiece, McGraw-Hill, 1973</ref> on plasma physics with [[Alvin Trivelpiece]] and in 1973 he won a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]].  He was a visiting professor at the [[University of California, San Diego]] and became a vice president at Science Applications, Inc. until 1978.  He made contributions to the plasma behavior in [[Tokamak]]s and [[Stellarator]]s.<ref>"Effect of turbulence on theta pinch modeling by hybrid numerical models" HAMASAKI, S; KRALL, NA, Laboratory for Applied science applications, Phys. Fluids 20, 65 (1977)</ref><ref>Turbulent heating studies in a tokamak P. L. Mascheroni, N. A. Krall, R. Bengtson, T. Kochanski, J. Jancarik, P. Phillips, and R. Stinnett, Phys. Fluids 22, 347 (1979)</ref><ref>"Electron ring startup model for ELMO Bumpy Torus"  S. Hamasaki, N. A. Krall, and J. L. Sperling, Phys. Fluids 27, 1759 (1984)</ref> He was appointed chairman of the [[United States Department of Energy|US Department of Energy]]'s [[Office of Science]] committee on alternate fusion concepts in 1977.  He became executive vice president and chief scientist at Jaycor Inc in 1978 and held that position until at least 1985.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://sbirsource.com/sbir/awards/118182-monitoring-energetic-a-particles-in-a-fusion-device |title=MONITORING ENERGETIC A-PARTICLES IN a FUSION DEVICE - Jaycor, Inc. - SBIR Source |access-date=2013-06-19 |archive-date=2015-05-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150527232208/https://sbirsource.com/sbir/awards/118182-monitoring-energetic-a-particles-in-a-fusion-device |url-status=dead }}</ref> He co-founded (with [[Stephen O Dean|Stephen O. Dean]] and [[Alvin Trivelpiece]]) the Fusion Power Associates, a Washington-based non for profit organization in 1979 and served as board chairman in 1983.<ref name="American"/><ref>{{Cite web | title=Fusion Power Associates | url=http://fusionpower.org/ | access-date=2025-11-24 | website=fusionpower.org}}</ref> In 1980 he served as chairman of division of plasma physics for the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>APS letters "Complaint over the fusion energy foundation" 12/16/1980</ref> In January 1988, he formed a consulting firm, Krall Associates.{{cn|date=October 2022}} He consulted with [[Robert W. Bussard]] in the late 1980s and early 1990s on [[Polywell]] research.<ref>Krall, N. A.; Coleman, M.; Maffei, K.; Lovberg, J.; Jacobsen, R.; Bussard, R. W. (1995). "Forming and maintaining a potential well in a quasispherical magnetic trap". Physics of Plasmas 2: 146.</ref>

He was twice married and was the father of six children and grandfather of nine. In retirement he continued contributing to research within his field.<ref name="American"/>

Krall died on January 17, 2026, at the age of 93.<ref>{{cite web |title=Nicholas Anthony Krall |url=https://www.dignitymemorial.com/obituaries/encinitas-ca/nicholas-krall-12716169 |website=Dignity Memorial |access-date=24 January 2026}}</ref>
